chunk_findings.detail: The new check is inserted into the shared record path and refuses command-gate `passed` records for which `evidence.ran_by` is empty. However, the only place setting `evidence.ran_by` is `ddflow ci run` (`ddflow/api/cirun.py`); the `ddflow gate run` path is unchanged and still leaves `ran_by` at its default `""`. A legitimate `ddflow gate run <id> <command_gate>` that executes the command successfully will produce evidence with `command` and `exit_code=0` but no `ran_by`, so `HR.hand_record` will classify it as a hand record and refuse it. This regresses the primary way a command gate is passed. The manifest confirms `gate run` is exercised by `tests/test_gate_run_after_merge.py` (modified in this change) but no corresponding `ran_by` assignment was added for that path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gates.py:1198-1204 (HR.hand_record call)

chunk_findings.detail: The refusal is gated on `agent_why` being truthy, so a never-run command gate is still accepted when no reason text is supplied. The bug's own repro, `ddflow gate record <id> unit_tests --outcome passed --command 'pytest -q' --exit-code 0`, has no `--reason`, so this line returns `""` immediately, `hand_record` returns `("", {})`, and the unit_tests gate is still recorded as passed with no run. The change therefore does not close Bed643a611b for the exact input it claims to fix.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/handrecord.py:20

chunk_findings.detail: The hand-record setup in `test_gate_record_keeps_the_output_file_it_digests` clears only `CLAUDECODE`, but the companion autouse fixture in `tests/test_gate_econ_tests.py` explicitly clears both `CLAUDECODE` and `DDFLOW_AGENT` because the suite itself may run under an agent harness. Under an environment with `DDFLOW_AGENT` set, this test still looks like an agent to the new `handrecord.py` refusal path, so the `gate record --command` call it makes is refused instead of accepted as a person’s hand record, causing the test to fail in exactly the supported agent-harness environment the change is meant to handle.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_gate_output_evidence.py:82

chunk_findings.detail: `_setup` configures `unit_tests` with `command = {sys.executable} -c "print('1 passed')"`, while `HAND` supplies `--command "pytest -q"`. The regression test therefore does not reproduce Bed643a611b as stated, where the recorded `--command` belongs to the configured, never-run gate. A faulty fix that rejects only when the supplied `--command` differs from the configured command would satisfy `test_an_agent_cannot_hand_record_a_never_run_command_gate_passed`, while still accepting the original bug when the recorded command matches the configured command. The test should arrange the configured command and the recorded command to be the same (or otherwise exercise a matching command) to ensure the refusal is truly caused by the no-run rule.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_gate_record_by_hand_command.py:28-38

chunk_findings.detail: This test calls `_setup(repo, monkeypatch)` with no claim argument, so it never calls `ddflow claim T1`. Since the sibling test explicitly uses `_setup(repo, monkeypatch, "--no-worktree")` to create a no-tree state, a normal claim is what would produce the tree that this first test asserts: `assert ev["tree_sha"] and "tree_sha" not in ev.get("unmeasured", [])`. Without that claim, the fixed code records `tree_sha` as unmeasured/absent, so the test fails on the intended behavior.

chunk_findings.detail:
`ran_by` is added as a plain, caller-visible field on `Evidence`, and line 1060 serializes any truthy `evidence.ran_by` into the stored evidence. The comment claims this value is “never by a flag or an MCP argument,” but nothing in this change marks the field as internal, excludes it from the tool schema, or rejects a caller-supplied value. If the `gate record` API/MCP binding exposes `Evidence` fields by name, an agent can reproduce the original bug with  
`ddflow gate record <id> unit_tests --outcome passed --command 'pytest -q' --exit-code 0 --ran-by 'ddflow ci run'`  
because the forged string is indistinguishable from the value set by `cirun.py`. The provenance/trust field is therefore just another attacker-controllable claim unless the record entrypoint refuses it at the boundary.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gates.py:852

chunk_findings.detail: The refusal guard is `if outcome != "passed" or not agent_why or gdef is None or not gdef.is_command_gate: return ""`. This makes an empty `agent_why` an automatic bypass of the entire verification. For the original repro, `ddflow gate record <id> unit_tests --outcome passed --command 'pytest -q' --exit-code 0` has no `--reason`, so if `agent_why` is the reason string, `_refusal` returns `""` immediately; `hand_record` then returns `("", _gaps(...))` and the never-run command gate is still recorded as passed. Even without the CLI mapping, any caller can invoke `hand_record(it, gdef, "unit_tests", "passed", "", tree, evidence, host, skip=False)` with an empty explanation and bypass the new refusal. An empty explanation should not disable trust verification; the condition should not include `or not agent_why`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/handrecord.py:20

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test does not verify the actual value, only that `ev["output_file_host"]` is truthy. An implementation that stores any non-empty placeholder (for example `"localhost"` or `"/tmp"`) would pass, even though the intent is to name the host that holds the output file. Likewise, the assertion only checks that `unmeasured` is a superset of `{"elapsed_s", "command_digest"}`; it never asserts those keys are absent from `ev`, so an implementation that still records `elapsed_s` and `command_digest` while also listing them in `unmeasured` would pass and leave the original “silently missing fields” bug partially in place.

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion assumes `by` contains at least one hyphen. In the same change’s other test the recording agent is `"a1"` (see `test_the_ran_by_provenance_cannot_be_typed_by_a_caller`), and the gate’s `by` field is that agent id, `"a1"`, which has no hyphen. Then `"a1".rsplit("-", 1)[1]` raises `IndexError`, causing the test to fail even when the measured-fields behavior is correct. The test should handle a hyphen-less `by` value or derive the expected suffix without indexing into a potentially single-element split.

chunk_findings.detail: The report still trusts the **presence** of `ran_by` rather than the trusted **value** allowlist that `ddflow/services/gates/handrecord.py` defines as `RAN_BY = {"ddflow ci run"}`. A record whose evidence contains an untrusted provenance value such as `"typed by an agent"` (the exact value the new handrecord test treats as untrusted) would make `report_gates._row(..., evidence={"ran_by": "typed by an agent"})["by_hand"]` be `False`. That is wrong because `hand_record` declares any value other than `"ddflow ci run"` “not trusted”; the report heuristic therefore still labels untrusted provenance as tool-produced instead of treating/refusing it as a hand record.

chunk_findings.detail: The hand-record setup in `test_gate_record_keeps_the_output_file_it_digests` clears only `CLAUDECODE`, but the companion autouse fixture in `tests/test_gate_econ_tests.py` explicitly clears both `CLAUDECODE` and `DDFLOW_AGENT` because the suite itself may run under an agent harness. Under an environment with `DDFLOW_AGENT` set, this test still looks like an agent to the new `handrecord.py` refusal path, so the `gate record --command` call it makes is refused instead of accepted as a person’s hand record, causing the test to fail in exactly the supported agent-harness environment the change is meant to handle.

chunk_findings.detail: `_setup` configures `unit_tests` with `command = {sys.executable} -c "print('1 passed')"`, while `HAND` supplies `--command "pytest -q"`. The regression test therefore does not reproduce Bed643a611b as stated, where the recorded `--command` belongs to the configured, never-run gate. A faulty fix that rejects only when the supplied `--command` differs from the configured command would satisfy `test_an_agent_cannot_hand_record_a_never_run_command_gate_passed`, while still accepting the original bug when the recorded command matches the configured command. The test should arrange the configured command and the recorded command to be the same (or otherwise exercise a matching command) to ensure the refusal is truly caused by the no-run rule.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_gate_record_by_hand_command.py:28-38

chunk_findings.detail: This test calls `_setup(repo, monkeypatch)` with no claim argument, so it never calls `ddflow claim T1`. Since the sibling test explicitly uses `_setup(repo, monkeypatch, "--no-worktree")` to create a no-tree state, a normal claim is what would produce the tree that this first test asserts: `assert ev["tree_sha"] and "tree_sha" not in ev.get("unmeasured", [])`. Without that claim, the fixed code records `tree_sha` as unmeasured/absent, so the test fails on the intended behavior.

chunk_findings.detail: The report still trusts the **presence** of `ran_by` rather than the trusted **value** allowlist that `ddflow/services/gates/handrecord.py` defines as `RAN_BY = {"ddflow ci run"}`. A record whose evidence contains an untrusted provenance value such as `"typed by an agent"` (the exact value the new handrecord test treats as untrusted) would make `report_gates._row(..., evidence={"ran_by": "typed by an agent"})["by_hand"]` be `False`. That is wrong because `hand_record` declares any value other than `"ddflow ci run"` “not trusted”; the report heuristic therefore still labels untrusted provenance as tool-produced instead of treating/refusing it as a hand record.

chunk_findings.detail:
`ran_by` is added as a plain, caller-visible field on `Evidence`, and line 1060 serializes any truthy `evidence.ran_by` into the stored evidence. The comment claims this value is “never by a flag or an MCP argument,” but nothing in this change marks the field as internal, excludes it from the tool schema, or rejects a caller-supplied value. If the `gate record` API/MCP binding exposes `Evidence` fields by name, an agent can reproduce the original bug with  
`ddflow gate record <id> unit_tests --outcome passed --command 'pytest -q' --exit-code 0 --ran-by 'ddflow ci run'`  
because the forged string is indistinguishable from the value set by `cirun.py`. The provenance/trust field is therefore just another attacker-controllable claim unless the record entrypoint refuses it at the boundary.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gates.py:852

chunk_findings.detail: The refusal guard is `if outcome != "passed" or not agent_why or gdef is None or not gdef.is_command_gate: return ""`. This makes an empty `agent_why` an automatic bypass of the entire verification. For the original repro, `ddflow gate record <id> unit_tests --outcome passed --command 'pytest -q' --exit-code 0` has no `--reason`, so if `agent_why` is the reason string, `_refusal` returns `""` immediately; `hand_record` then returns `("", _gaps(...))` and the never-run command gate is still recorded as passed. Even without the CLI mapping, any caller can invoke `hand_record(it, gdef, "unit_tests", "passed", "", tree, evidence, host, skip=False)` with an empty explanation and bypass the new refusal. An empty explanation should not disable trust verification; the condition should not include `or not agent_why`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/handrecord.py:20

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test does not verify the actual value, only that `ev["output_file_host"]` is truthy. An implementation that stores any non-empty placeholder (for example `"localhost"` or `"/tmp"`) would pass, even though the intent is to name the host that holds the output file. Likewise, the assertion only checks that `unmeasured` is a superset of `{"elapsed_s", "command_digest"}`; it never asserts those keys are absent from `ev`, so an implementation that still records `elapsed_s` and `command_digest` while also listing them in `unmeasured` would pass and leave the original “silently missing fields” bug partially in place.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_gate_record_measured_fields.py:56,58

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test only attempts to pass `--ran-by` as a CLI flag; it never exercises the MCP/API binding where `Evidence` fields are passed by name, which was the root cause. An implementation that still accepts a caller-supplied `ran_by` through a named argument in the `gate record` MCP call would pass this test unchanged, because that code path is never invoked. The test therefore does not verify the intended fix and allows the original vulnerability to remain undetected.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_gate_record_by_hand_command.py:test_the_ran_by_provenance_cannot_be_typed_by_a_caller

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion assumes `by` contains at least one hyphen. In the same change’s other test the recording agent is `"a1"` (see `test_the_ran_by_provenance_cannot_be_typed_by_a_caller`), and the gate’s `by` field is that agent id, `"a1"`, which has no hyphen. Then `"a1".rsplit("-", 1)[1]` raises `IndexError`, causing the test to fail even when the measured-fields behavior is correct. The test should handle a hyphen-less `by` value or derive the expected suffix without indexing into a potentially single-element split.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_gate_record_measured_fields.py:assert ev["output_file_host"].endswith("-proj-" + by.rsplit("-", 1)[1])

chunk_findings.detail: The added regression test only inspects the MCP tool schema’s `properties` dict and asserts `"ran_by"`/`"ran-by"` is absent. It never sends an actual `ddflow_gate_record` MCP call with an extra `ran_by` argument, nor asserts that such an undeclared property is rejected or ignored by the binding. An implementation whose handler still accepts `Evidence` fields through `**kwargs`, or whose MCP validator leaves `additionalProperties` at JSON Schema’s default true, passes this test unchanged, so the caller-controlled `ran_by` path from the original bug remains unexercised.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_gate_record_by_hand_command.py:test_the_mcp_gate_record_tool_has_no_ran_by_argument

chunk_findings.detail: The added regression block only calls `report_gates._row` with `ran_by="typed"`; it still never exercises the `ddflow gate record` MCP/API binding where `Evidence` fields are passed by name. An implementation that still accepts a caller-supplied `ran_by` named argument unchanged would pass this test unchanged. The author’s triage claims `test_the_mcp_gate_record_tool_has_no_ran_by_argument` was added, but that test is not present in this visible diff, so this previously confirmed test-gap still holds.

data.summary: ddflow ci run lock has no fairness: with many agents, gate run ci starves. Three consecutive gate run ci attempts (about 30 min wait each) ended 'blocked on <sha> of <repo> (pid N)' -> unavailable, because other agents' ci runs kept taking the repo-wide ci lock (no FIFO). The waiter holds its file lease throughout, so agents waiting on it get YIELD REQUESTED. Fix: FIFO ticket order for ci runs (or keep a blocked run's place across retries) and print the queue position.

data.body:
Fixes bug B1fa77a6832: ddflow ci run lock has no fairness: with many agents, gate run ci starves. Three consecutive gate run ci attempts (about 30 min wait each) ended 'blocked on <sha> of <repo> (pid N)' -> unavailable, because other agents' ci runs kept taking the repo-wide ci lock (no FIFO). The waiter holds its file lease throughout, so agents waiting on it get YIELD REQUESTED. Fix: FIFO ticket order for ci runs (or keep a blocked run's place across retries) and print the queue position.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B1fa77a6832 --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed B1fa77a6832 --regression-test <test>` first).
